reading.body:
Flexential Denver - Englewood publishes 18 MW of IT capacity across 240,549 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 18 MW supports roughly 450 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation average, the same power supports roughly 1,800 racks. The operator has not published a rack count, a power density target, or a cooling architecture, so which end of that range applies here is not determinable from the spec page.

The seven certifications cover distinct requirements. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify the facility for regulated financial and operational workloads. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR qualifies it for export-controlled defense and aerospace data. NIST 800-53 aligns it with federal security controls. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. SSAE 18 is the auditing standard under which the SOC reports are issued, not a separate operational credential. Together these certifications make the campus eligible to host a wide range of compliance-sensitive workloads, but which tenants are actually present is not published.

Among the 17 Colorado facilities this site has mapped, Englewood is ranked first by published IT capacity, and it accounts for all 18 MW of the published total for the state. That ranking is an artifact of disclosure, not necessarily of physical scale: only one of the 17 mapped facilities publishes a megawatt figure, so 16 sites contribute nothing to the comparison. Colorado sits within reach of large Rocky Mountain renewable generation, but grid interconnection details and power sources for this campus are not published in the operator's specifications.
